problem: Earlier this week, HAL made a music video that passed every automated check. Its owner watched it once and called it bad.
loop_note: Today's direction: glitchy experimental trap, lyrics by HAL in the owner's themes, emo-trap inspiration turned into musical traits. Artist names are refused in prompts.
create_note: Every call carries one session tag, so Livepeer Agent's cost report is the production's receipt: $21.61 for the whole song and video, 49 calls.
review_lines: Lyrics: every take transcribed from its separated vocal. 98-100% of lines sung, word error 0.16-0.23.
Lip-sync: the audio in every returned clip is cross-correlated with the vocal segment sent. Offset 0 ms on all eight.
Edit: every cut on a bar line of the song's own beat grid; no cut longer than its shot.
Master: EQ, width, glue compression, a soft clipper and an oversampled limiter to -10 LUFS, peaks safe after AAC.
Style and timing gates for remakes: a MuQ-MuLan fingerprint against the owner's catalog, beats within 40 ms.
taste: Today's first cut passed every check. The owner watched it and asked for lip-sync, real typography, and the look of the artists the owner follows.
taste_fix: HAL studied those videos and rebuilt the edit: lip-synced performance from two angles, a real master, kick-and-snare effects. The owner's verdict counts three times as much as any score.
result_line: Lyrics by HAL, sung by MiniMax Music 3, picture by FLUX, Kling and OmniHuman, all through Livepeer Agent. Cut on the beat by HAL Studio.
close: Apache-2.0. Studio code, tests, and the receipt for every Livepeer Agent call are in the folder above.
